subject: Locale quality sprint proposal + demo ops
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@polylingo.com>, Jin Park <jin@polylingo.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Locale quality sprint proposal + demo ops

Hi Sophie / Jin —

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning. High-level recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- What we heard: PolyLingo needs a pilot to validate model suitability across EN/FR/DE (EU focus) and JA/KO (APAC add-on). Key concerns are fidelity for formal/legal copy in FR/DE, and hallucination rate on short-form QA in JA/KO.
- Acceptance criteria (your ask): per-locale accuracy >= 92% on the legal-copy testset; hallucination incidence < 3% on the short-form QA slice; median token-latency < 120ms at 8k context in our Dedicated config.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Locale-quality sprint (3 weeks): Redwood will run a bench suite on a shortlisted model set, surface per-locale metrics + example failure modes, and provide a prompt-set pack for your in-house reviewers.
2) Pilot scope: 50k tokens/day for 2 weeks on Dedicated with automated KV-caching enabled.
3) Deliverables: benchmark report, prompt-set bundle (EN/FR/DE/JA/KO), open issues log with regression risk flags, and a demo session to walk results.

I've attached a one-page evaluation plan and an initial prompt bundle. Neha will lead the eval and Ben will run the Dedicated sizing estimate. Can you confirm sample datasets and a preferred date for the demo (we suggest 09/23 or 09/24)?

Thanks — I’ll set up a follow-up calendar once we hear back.

Best,
Markus
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: polylingo-eval-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf), prompt-set-EN-FR-JA.tar.gz (archive)
From: Sophie Martin <sophie@polylingo.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jin Park <jin@polylingo.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 02:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Locale quality sprint proposal + demo ops

Markus —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers: 
- We can provide two anonymized sample sets by EOD 9/15: (1) Legal boilerplate (FR/DE) ~1.2K sentences; (2) Customer QA transcripts (JA/KO) ~800 snippets.
- Demo preferred 09/23 morning CET.

Couple of clarifications from our side: 
- Can the benchmark include a regression delta relative to our current vendor (we can share slices)? We want explicit delta numbers, not just absolute metrics.
- For the hallucination definition: we classify a hallucination as any generated fact that cannot be corroborated by the vendor dataset or the prompt context. Will Redwood match that definition?

Also looping in Jin for infra constraints and to confirm we can open a temporary S3 share for sample artifacts.

— Sophie
Head of Localization
PolyLingo
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@polylingo.com>, Jin Park <jin@polylingo.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Locale quality sprint proposal + demo ops

Hi Sophie / Jin —

Great — appreciate the sample commitment. Quick technical notes / commitments from Redwood for the sprint: 

- Model shortlist: we will evaluate three variants: 1) OpenLM L-7BFP16 (baseline fast path), 2) Redwood-Tuned-13B-q4 (quantized medium), 3) OpenChain-70B-INT8 (high-quality variant). Each checkpoint will be profiled for per-locale precision/recall and hallucination classification.
- Regression metric: we will compute per-locale delta against your vendor slices as absolute % points and produce a nightly diff report during the sprint.
- Prompt sets: we will include a conservative (safety-first) and an aggressive (fluency-first) variant per locale; both are in the attached bundle.
- Quality flags: examples will be tagged with one of {fluency_issue, factual_hallucination, tone_mismatch, tokenizer_artifact}. We note that JA/KO tokenization creates more truncation edge cases — we will surface sample failure cases with KV cache state to reproduce the issue.

Operational asks for PolyLingo: 
- Please provide the two sample sets to s3://redwood-eval-temp/PL-2027-09-MK1 or share a presigned URL by 09/15.
- Confirm demo slot 09/23 09:00 CET (we’ll send an invite).

Ben — can you drop the Dedicated sizing estimate and expected token-latency for the three variants in this thread? I’ll assemble the benchmark harness and schedule the runs.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt-set-EN-FR-DE-JA-KO-v2.zip (zip)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Sophie Martin <sophie@polylingo.com>, Jin Park <jin@polylingo.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Locale quality sprint proposal + demo ops

Quick sizing note —

- Dedicated config suggestion (pilot): 2 x A100 80GB-equivalent (shared pool) with autoscale burst to 3 instances for peak runs. Estimated median token-latency (8k context):
  - OpenLM L-7BFP16: 68ms median
  - Redwood-Tuned-13B-q4: 103ms median
  - OpenChain-70B-INT8: 185ms median

- Cost estimate for 2-week pilot at 50k tokens/day: ~$9.5k (compute + logging + storage). We can reduce cost by enabling prefix caching for the legal boilerplate (expected 18–24% token cost reduction).

I’ll provision a temporary S3 bucket and share creds with Sophie/Jin when samples arrive. Also included a short runbook for the demo (link below).

Runbook + results link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/1a2b3c-eval-pack

Ben
Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
